Tableau x AI

Tableau has always given people a way to see their data clearly — and that foundation now powers something far more expansive. What was once a platform for building and sharing visualizations has evolved into a truly agentic analytic experience: one that explores alongside you, surfaces the narrative behind the numbers, and proactively uncovers insight before you even know to look for it.

Built-in detection engines continuously scan for meaningful signals, while conversational analytics lets anyone engage with data in plain language and get a governed, trustworthy answer in return. It's what makes Tableau the governed analytics platform built for the agentic era.

From built-in AI to headless analytics, let's take a tour through Tableau's ever evolving platform that enables every organisation to turn trusted knowledge into action.

Tableau Knowledge

Meet Tableau Knowledge, the enterprise knowledge management solution that unifies all of your data assets into live knowledge graphs that your team can explore and enrich, and make accessible to any AI agent.

1

Navigate to Tableau Knowledge

From the Tableau Home page, click Tableau Knowledge in the left navigation bar.

2

Explore the Default Graph

Open the Default knowledge graph and review the assets available: Data Sources, Workbooks, Views and other content.

3

Search for fun content

Try searching for: Music, Film, Football, Cars, Media. Can you find all five? Why not?

Permissions in Tableau Cloud still apply inside Knowledge. If you don't have access to a data source, it won't appear in the knowledge graph either. Different user accounts can see different subsets of the fun content.
4

Find the workshop Data Source

Search for SaaS Revenue and Retention. Click through to the associated workbook and drill into the elements: fields, relationships and lineage.

5

Upload a Business Preferences file

Download the SaaS Business Preferences PDF, then upload it as an asset in the knowledge graph: + → Add Business Preferences → Upload Document.

📄 SaaS Bookings & Retention Business Preferences

SaaS Bookings & Retention · saas_bookings_retention_business_preferences.pdf · 172 KB

Business Preferences are scoped to 'Global (all entities)' at this time.

6

Check graph health

Return to the Knowledge home page and review the Health score for the Default graph. Then ask the agent:

"What do I need to do to improve the health of this knowledge graph?"

7

Create your own Knowledge Graph (if time permits)

Create a new Knowledge Graph and use Manage Sources to bring in content. Prefix your graph name with your name or initials so it doesn't clash with others. There is a maximum of 5 Knowledge Graphs on this site.

Hands-on

Tableau Agent in Pulse

Pulse pushes personalised insights into Slack, email and mobile. Tableau Agent lets you talk back: ask "why did this drop?" and get a plain-language answer, the drivers behind it and the next questions worth asking.

Getting there

From Tableau Home, click Tableau Pulse in the left navigation bar. Open the metric group SaaS Revenue and Retention and answer the questions below by drilling into the metrics, using Ask Q&A or Tableau Agent in Pulse.

1 · Breakdown

Which territories had the largest increase in Churned ARR last month?

Navigate to Churned ARR → breakdown by Territory

New York - Manhattan, New York - Brooklyn and Seattle each increased by about $2K compared with the previous month. Overall Churned ARR actually decreased by $17K: 5 of the 12 territories increased, and the other 7 fell by a combined $23K.
2 · ✦ Ask Q&A

Which territories are losing more ARR?

Stay in Churned ARR and open Ask. Select the suggested question.

Ask reads "losing more ARR" as higher Churned ARR (quarter to date) and ranks territories by it: New York - Brooklyn ($118K, 8.6% of the total) and Seattle ($110K, 8.0%) lead, with Orlando, Chicago, Schaumburg, Bellevue and Camarillo close behind ($75–92K).
It also compares with last quarter. Overall Churned ARR is down $58K, and the biggest improvements are the three New York territories: Manhattan (−$32K), White Plains (−$26K) and Brooklyn (−$16K). Seattle, Miami, Schaumburg, Bellevue and Camarillo actually got worse.
Use this to discuss level vs change: a territory can have high churn and still be improving.
3 · Tableau Agent in Pulse

Is retention keeping up with bookings, and what is driving the change in bookings?

Yes, retention is keeping up. In Q4 2026 quarter-to-date, Bookings is about $15M, down 2.5% on Q3 QTD, while Churned ARR is about $1M, down 4.1%. The softness is in new bookings, not retention. The biggest drags on Bookings are Core Platform (−$426K, −12.3%), Mid-Market (−$297K) and New York (−$474K, −9.7%), led by the territories Manhattan (−$183K), White Plains (−$151K) and Brooklyn (−$140K). Churned ARR improves in the same places (Core Platform −$64K, NY −$74K).
Pulse wording will vary from run to run, but the drivers should be the same.
4 · Discovery Sequence

Ask these questions in order using Tableau Agent in Pulse. Each builds on the last.

How have Bookings and Churned ARR changed this year compared with last year?

Which territories have the largest increase in Churned ARR this year compared with last year, and how does their Bookings growth compare?

Which product is driving it in those territories?

How have Deals Closed and Bookings changed there compared with Churned ARR?

What else changed in that product and those territories at the same time?

Bookings is up 9.9% YTD ($159M vs $145M) but Churned ARR is up 14.5%, and the gap is concentrated in three territories: Manhattan (+$586K Churned ARR), White Plains (+$462K) and Brooklyn (+$372K). In those territories Churned ARR is up 36–38% against Bookings up only 21–23%, while the other nine territories grow both by roughly 2–8%. Core Platform is the product driving it. The same product and territories had their discount rate jump from about 12% to about 30% in December 2025, so volume bought with discounts churned out almost as fast as it came in. The discounting stopped on 11 October 2026, and Q4 quarter-to-date Bookings and Churned ARR are now both falling.
Pulse follows its own previous answer, so check each step lands on the New York territories before moving on.
Tip for Tableau Agent questions
Don't name the territory or product you expect to be the answer. Naming one makes the agent filter every metric to it, which removes the benchmark it needs to compare against. Ask which one stands out and let the agent find it.

Hands-on

Conversational Analytics

Dashboard Narratives reads the dashboard for you and writes up the story. Conversational Analytics then lets you ask follow-up questions in natural language, grounded in the data behind the dashboard.

Choose your adventure

Navigate to the MIMECAST project in Explore and open the SaaS Revenue and Retention dashboard.

☁️
SaaS Revenue and Retention
Bookings, discounts, churn & support

Open Tableau Agent

With the dashboard open, click the Tableau Agent icon in the toolbar (top-right of the dashboard) and Got it. Start with Overview, then try Insights. Now ask the questions below.

1 · Validate

How many deals did we close in the last 4 weeks (7 September to 4 October 2026)?

Checks the agent can read the dashboard accurately.

The figure should match the Deals Closed tile: 92,316.
2 · Rank

Which territory was discounting the most in the last 4 weeks (7 September to 4 October 2026), looking at discounts as a share of gross bookings?

The agent builds a ratio per territory and ranks them. Three New York territories stand out: White Plains 15.0%, Brooklyn 14.6% and Manhattan 14.5%. The other nine sit at about 8.5%.
3 · Trend

How has the discount rate for Core Platform in NY moved month by month over the past year (October 2025 to September 2026)? When did it first go above 20%?

A monthly series the dashboard doesn't show: about 12% through November 2025, then December 2025 (23.5%), and about 30% from January 2026 onward.
4 · Complex

In Core Platform, which territories are growing seats much faster than the rest, and what happened to their discount rate? Compare January to September 2026 with January to September 2025.

Three territories stand out: White Plains seats +101%, Manhattan +92% and Brooklyn +86%, with discount rates up from about 12% to about 30%. The other nine territories grow seats 3–9% with discount rates unchanged at about 12%. A two-period, two-measure derived comparison.
5 · Hidden issue

Which state and product had an unusual spike in service incidents in 2026, and what happened to CSAT and bookings while it lasted?

WA Professional Services, April to July 2026: about 1,070 incidents vs about 100 in the same months of 2025, Avg CSAT down from 4.30 to 3.76, and bookings down about 19%. It recovered by August.
Tips for Dashboard Q&A
Ask the way you'd ask a colleague. Keep the period in every question ("in the last 4 weeks" plus the dates in brackets) so the agent doesn't count back from today. Say how a ratio is worked out so the agent and the dashboard use the same definition.
If you wanted the agent to always use the last 4 weeks, or you had a standard definition for ratio calculations, what could you change?
Business Preferences

Headless BI with Tableau MCP

The Tableau MCP lets Claude, or any AI agent, query your published data sources directly, using the same certified fields, calculations and permissions as your dashboards. First do what many people do today: drop a CSV export into an AI chat. Then connect Claude to Tableau, ask the same questions and compare the answers.

The experiment

You will ask the same two questions of two data sources and compare.
Data source 1 · the CSV export. Download it to your own computer, load it into your own Claude Desktop and ask two questions.
Connect Claude to Tableau. Add the Tableau MCP and sign in to the workshop Tableau Cloud site.
Data source 2 · the certified data source via the MCP. Ask the same questions, then ask Claude to explain every difference.

Before you start
Open Claude Desktop on your own computer (not the Hot Pass workspace). Claude needs code execution to analyse a CSV: check it's switched on under Settings → Capabilities. Keep your Tableau Cloud login handy.
Data source 1 · The CSV export
1 · Download the export

📊 SaaS dataset export

AI Workshop - Saas Dataset.csv · 72,000 rows · Jan 2024 – 10 Oct 2026

Download
2 · Ask Claude about the CSV

Here's an export of our data. Please answer: 1. How many deals have we closed so far this month (1–29 October 2026), and how does that compare with the same days last month (1–29 September 2026)? 2. Which product was our most profitable last month (September 2026), and how much profit did each product make?

Attach the CSV first, then paste this. Keep the chat open: you'll come back to it.

Connect Claude to Tableau
1

Log into Blender

Open

https://blender.demo.tableau.com/

and log in with the Tableau Cloud login you used earlier.

Data source 2 · The certified data source via the Tableau MCP
3 · Ask Tableau the same questions

Now use the Tableau MCP to answer the same questions from the certified SaaS Revenue and Retention data source on Tableau Cloud.

Use the same chat as the CSV, with Tableau switched on.

4 · Compare

Compare the answers from the CSV with the answers from Tableau in a table. For each difference, explain what caused it (out-of-date data, the wrong field or a different calculation) and tell me which answer I should trust.

Tableau (certified): 89,199 deals for 1–29 October vs 94,683 for 1–29 September (−5.8%).
CSV: The export stops on 10 October, so Claude only sees 1–10 October 2026: 34,943. Against 1–29 September that looks like −63.1%; even like-for-like against 1–10 September (31,561) it shows +10.7%, not the −5.8% for the whole period.
Out of date. The CSV is missing the last 19 days. The certified source is refreshed with the data.
September is complete in both sources, so the ranking is the same. The CSV has no profit column, so Claude builds its own. Using Gross Bookings − Discounts − Cost of Revenue: Core Platform $1.27M, Analytics $847K, Collaboration $834K, Security $796K, Integrations $692K, Professional Services $625K. If Claude leaves discounts out, Core Platform is still first but every figure is higher ($1.99M for Core Platform).
Own calculation. Neither source has a profit column, so check which definition Claude uses with each, and whether it tells you.

Hands-on

Build a Data App with Headless Analytics

A Data App is a custom web app that lives inside Tableau. It's HTML and JavaScript packaged into a workbook, and it queries a published data source live through the Tableau Extensions API. Because it's Tableau content, it's governed like any dashboard: it sits in a project, follows that project's permissions, always shows the current data and traces back to its source.

The plan

Vibe-code it. Claude designs a dashboard as an artifact, using the data it reaches through the Tableau MCP.

Publish it. Claude publishes the app to Tableau with the REST API, signed in as you.

Open it in Tableau. It's a new governed asset: owned, permissioned, always current.

Before you start
Stay in your Claude chat from the Headless section, with Tableau switched on. So that Claude's code can reach Tableau Cloud, open Settings → Capabilities and allow network access to blender.demo.tableau.com (add it as an allowed domain, or choose all domains).
1 · Vibe-code the dashboard

Using the Tableau MCP, list the data sources I can access and ask me which one to use. Then vibe-code a one-page dashboard from it as an HTML artifact: KPI tiles for the key measures so far this month against the same days last month; a weekly trend for the last 13 weeks; and a breakdown by the most useful dimension. Use real numbers from the data source, and open with a one-line headline that says what's happening.

Pick any data source you like, such as SaaS Revenue and Retention or one of the music, film, sport or cars datasets. Then make it yours, one sentence at a time: "make the trend a bar chart", "highlight anything below last month", "use our brand colours". The artifact is a snapshot: Claude copied the numbers in when it built it.

2 · Publish it to Tableau

Publish as a Data App

Log in with Blender, using the same login as earlier, and give Claude the Blender login when it asks. Claude signs in with the Tableau REST API, publishes the workbook to the MIMECAST project and gives you the link. Open it, and if Tableau asks whether to allow the extension, choose Allow.

Now look at it as Tableau content. It has an owner (you), lives in a project and follows that project's permissions. When the data source refreshes, the app shows the new numbers the next time it opens. Nothing needs re-exporting or re-publishing.

Hands-on

Tableau Studio

Tableau Studio lets you vibe-code with your data. Describe the dashboard you want in plain language, watch it build, then refine it one sentence at a time. You can also use the same conversation to investigate the data: ask what's unusual, why something spiked and what's driving a pattern, then ask for the chart that proves it. You'll do both: build a dashboard in minutes, then find the stories in your data.

Log in
Log in to Tableau Studio with the Tableau Cloud credentials you used earlier. Then pick a dataset: music, film, sport or cars.

The challenge

Vibe-code a dashboard. Start with the prompt below, then make it yours: "make the trend a bar chart", "add a filter for region", "highlight the top 3".
Turn detective. Use Insights, or ask Studio what stands out, then work through the insight hunt. Each dataset contains real patterns and a few genuine outliers.
Prove it. Every claim needs a number and a chart. Then present your best finding in a dashboard, or let Claude and the Tableau MCP write the data story.
No peeking. Every hunt has a Reveal insight button, and you have to click it twice to see the answer. Try at least two prompts of your own before you reveal it.

🎵 Music Streaming Charts
240 tracks · 6 regions · Oct 2024 – Sep 2026. Connect to the Music Streaming Charts data source in your BACKSTAGE project.
1 · Vibe-code

Build me a music streaming dashboard: KPI tiles for streams, unique listeners, revenue and average skip rate; a monthly streams trend; the top 10 artists and tracks; and a genre-by-region heat map.

One row = one track, in one region, in one month. Skip Rate is a rate, so average it rather than summing it.

2 · Discover

What are the three most surprising things in this data? Show me a chart for each and tell me why it matters.

Then push back: "Why?" and "Is that a real pattern or a quirk of the data?" The best insights come from the second and third question.

3 · Insight hunt

7 stories are hiding in this data. Turn each question into your own prompt. The hint shows one way to ask it.

🎄Is there a genre that only shows up for part of the year?

Try monthly streams by genre. Does any genre behave differently from the rest?

Christmas. Christmas tracks are near-silent from January to October, then jump to ~8M streams in November and ~33M in December, about 12% of all December streams. A yearly total hides this completely.

🚀Which track grew the fastest this year, and which other measure moved with it?

Compare growth rather than totals, then look at Shares per 1,000 streams.

"Quiet Highway (17)" by Tomás Iglesias. A forgotten track streaming ~0.15M a month jumps to 3.1M by April 2026 (~20x). Shares per 1,000 streams leap from ~4 to ~17–19 at the same time, which is the viral signal. It settles at ~1M a month, still 6x its old level.

🕯️Did any artist have one month that looks nothing like the rest? What might have happened?

Plot monthly streams by artist and look for a single spike.

Dale Whitaker, July 2025. ~49.5M streams against ~6M in a typical month (8x), for one month only. A one-off spike across a whole catalogue usually means a news event, such as a tribute, an anniversary or a film sync.

🌍Does where a listener lives change what they listen to?

Show each genre's share of streams by region, not total streams.

Three home-turf genres. Latin earns 38% of its streams in Latin America, K-Pop 48% in Asia and Country 51% in North America. Every other genre splits roughly 17% / 24% / 25% across those regions.

⏭️What makes listeners hit skip?

Compare average Skip Rate by Explicit, Duration (Sec) and Genre.

Explicit and long tracks. Explicit tracks are skipped 30% of the time vs 23% for clean ones. Tracks over 4:20 (260 sec) are skipped 35% of the time vs 24% for shorter tracks.

💰Who earns more for every 1,000 streams: major or independent labels?

Build a ratio: SUM(Revenue) ÷ SUM(Streams) × 1,000, by Label Type.

Independent labels earn US$4.09 per 1,000 streams vs US$3.20 for majors, about 28% more per play. Majors still win on total revenue because they have far more streams.

📉Is the platform growing?

Trend total streams by month, then compare streams per track by Track Age (Months).

No. Monthly streams fall from 134M (Oct 2024) to 83M (Sep 2026), down ~38%. Tracks in their first six months average ~16M streams vs ~3–4M for older tracks, so the platform depends on a steady flow of new releases.
4 · Present it

Using the Tableau MCP, connect to the Music Streaming Charts data source and find the three most surprising insights in it. For each one, give me a headline, the key number and a chart, as a one-page HTML data story.

Paste this into Claude with the Tableau MCP connected. Claude queries your published data source directly. Does it find the same stories you did?

🎬 Film Box Office
3,000 films · 2005 – 2025 · 5 regions. Connect to the Film Box Office data source in your BACKSTAGE project.
1 · Vibe-code

Build me a box office dashboard: KPI tiles for box office, budget and ROI (box office ÷ budget); box office by release year; the top 10 films; ROI by genre; and critic vs audience score as a scatter plot.

One row = one film in one region. Budget and Box Office are split by region, so SUM them per film. Use Release Date for month order, because Release Month is text and sorts alphabetically.

2 · Discover

What are the three most surprising things in this data? Show me a chart for each and tell me why it matters.

Then push back: "Why?" and "Is that a real pattern or a quirk of the data?" The best insights come from the second and third question.

3 · Insight hunt

7 stories are hiding in this data. Turn each question into your own prompt. The hint shows one way to ask it.

💸Which film made the most money for every dollar spent, and which lost the most?

Build ROI as SUM(Box Office) ÷ SUM(Budget), and profit as Box Office − Budget, for each film.

Best ROI: "Basement Tape (found footage)", a US$0.15M horror that grossed US$190M (~1,275x). Biggest loss: "Pirate Gold 5: Cursed Ledger", with a US$350M budget, a US$40M gross (−US$310M) and a critic score of 21. The top grosser overall is "Galactic Mega-Saga: Endgame Run" at US$2.7bn.

🍅Do critics and audiences ever completely disagree?

Plot Critic Score against Audience Score for each film and look for the biggest gap.

"Quiet Fields". Critics give it 96 and audiences 41, the biggest gap in the data. It's also the lowest-grossing film of all (US$0.4M on a US$9M budget). Critics loved it, and almost nobody went to see it.

📅Is there a best and a worst month to release a film? Is it the same for Horror?

Use the month of Release Date and compare average box office per film, then filter to Horror.

May, June and December average ~US$320–340M per film. September (~US$160M) and January (~US$190M) earn the least. Horror breaks the rule: its October total is about 2x any other month. Halloween.

🦠Was there a period when cinemas went quiet? Has the industry recovered?

Trend total box office by Release Year.

2020 and 2021 take ~US$15bn each, against ~US$40–50bn in a normal year. That's the pandemic dip. 2022–2024 bounce back to normal levels.

🔁Are sequels better, or just bigger?

Compare average Critic Score, Audience Score and Box Office per film for Sequel vs New.

Just bigger. Sequels score lower with critics (57 vs 63) but gross about double (average US$483M vs US$228M per film). Audiences are kinder to franchise films than critics are (~69 vs ~59).

🔞Does the age rating change how much a film earns?

Compare median ROI per film by Rating.

Yes. G-rated films return a median 3.3x their budget, PG 2.1x, PG-13 1.8x and R-rated 1.3x. A bigger potential audience means a better return.

🏆Which genre wins the awards, and does it make money?

Compare Awards Nominations and median ROI by Genre.

Drama collects 48% of all award nominations but has the worst median ROI (~1.0x, so it barely breaks even). Animation has the best (3.4x). Prestige and profit rarely go together.
4 · Present it

Using the Tableau MCP, connect to the Film Box Office data source and find the three most surprising insights in it. For each one, give me a headline, the key number and a chart, as a one-page HTML data story.

Paste this into Claude with the Tableau MCP connected. Claude queries your published data source directly. Does it find the same stories you did?

⚽ Football League Matches
5 fictional leagues · 8 seasons · 15,200 matches. Connect to the Football League Matches data source in your BACKSTAGE project.
1 · Vibe-code

Build me a football league dashboard: a league table (points, wins, goal difference) filtered by league and season; wage bill vs points as a scatter plot; home vs away points per match; and goals per match by league.

One row = one team's view of one match, so there are two rows per match. League table = SUM(Points) by Team and Season. Attendance is only recorded on home rows.

2 · Discover

What are the three most surprising things in this data? Show me a chart for each and tell me why it matters.

Then push back: "Why?" and "Is that a real pattern or a quirk of the data?" The best insights come from the second and third question.

3 · Insight hunt

6 stories are hiding in this data. Turn each question into your own prompt. The hint shows one way to ask it.

💷Does money buy titles? How often does the biggest spender win the league?

Build a league table (SUM(Points) by Team and Season), then compare each champion's wage bill with the rest of its league.

Mostly, yes. Points and wage bill move together strongly (correlation ~0.79 across team-seasons), and the biggest spender wins 23 of the 40 league titles.

🧚Is there a champion that money can't explain?

Plot wage bill against points for every champion, or rank champions by wage bill.

Premier County, 2021/22. They have the lowest wage bill in the Premier Division (US$10.5M vs a median of ~US$87M) and score 5–20 points in every other season, yet they win the title with 95 points, then drop straight back. The ultimate outlier.

👑Does any club dominate its league for years?

Count league titles by team for each league.

Premier Argyle, the Premier Division's biggest spender, wins 6 of the 8 titles. One of the two seasons they miss is the year Premier County shocks everyone.

🏟️How much is home advantage worth, and was there a season it almost vanished? Why?

Compare average Points per match for Home vs Away by Season, then bring in Attendance.

Home teams average ~1.8 points a match vs ~1.0 away. In 2020/21 the gap shrinks from ~0.8 to 0.28, the season stadiums were almost empty (an average home crowd of 659 vs ~29,500). Crowds are a big part of home advantage.

🟥What does a red card cost a team?

Compare average Points, xG and xG Against for matches with and without a red card.

Teams with a red card average 0.89 points vs 1.42 without one, and the opposition's expected goals (xG Against) jump from 1.38 to 1.84. Down to ten players, a team spends the rest of the match defending.

🎉Which league is the most entertaining to watch?

Compare average Goals For per team per match by League.

Rhein Liga scores the most (1.56 goals per team per match) and Ligue Océan the fewest (1.31).
4 · Present it

Using the Tableau MCP, connect to the Football League Matches data source and find the three most surprising insights in it. For each one, give me a headline, the key number and a chart, as a one-page HTML data story.

Paste this into Claude with the Tableau MCP connected. Claude queries your published data source directly. Does it find the same stories you did?

🚗 Used Car Market
30,000 listings · 22 makes · 2024 – 2025. Connect to the Used Car Market data source in your BACKSTAGE project.
1 · Vibe-code

Build me a used car market dashboard: KPI tiles for listings, median price and median days on market; value retained by age for each fuel type; average price by make; price vs odometer as a scatter plot; and listings by state.

One row = one listing. Value Retained % = Listing Price ÷ Original MSRP, so average it and never sum it.

2 · Discover

What are the three most surprising things in this data? Show me a chart for each and tell me why it matters.

Then push back: "Why?" and "Is that a real pattern or a quirk of the data?" The best insights come from the second and third question.

3 · Insight hunt

6 stories are hiding in this data. Turn each question into your own prompt. The hint shows one way to ask it.

🔋Which kind of car loses value the fastest?

Plot average Value Retained % by Age (Years), with one line per Fuel Type.

Electric cars. Their median value retained is 25% vs ~43% for petrol, diesel and hybrid. At 5–8 years old they keep ~17% vs ~35%. The Nissan Leaf fares worst (11%), then Kia (23%) and Tesla (28%).

📈Is any car worth more today than when it was new? Which ones, and why?

Filter to Value Retained % above 100%, then look at Make, Model and Year.

Two groups. Classics: ~240 pre-1990 cars (Corvette, HiLux, Wrangler, 911, F-150, Mini, Mustang) list at a median ~2.7x their original price, and the priciest listings in the data are 1970s–80s Porsche 911s at ~US$650K. Modern supercars: Porsche 911s and Lamborghini Huracáns from 2016 or earlier are the only post-1990 cars worth more than new.

⚠️Does any model have a model year that's out of step with the rest?

Plot Value Retained % by Year with one line per model, and look for a dip that breaks the curve.

Fiat 500, 2016–17. Those model years keep only 8–10% of their value vs 14% for 2015 and 26% for 2018. That looks like a recall or reliability scare hitting resale prices.

🎨Does colour matter when you sell?

Compare average Value Retained % by Colour.

A little, consistently. Orange, yellow and white cars hold the most value. Gold and brown hold the least.

⏱️Which cars sell fastest, and which sit on the lot?

Compare median Days on Market by Make and by Fuel Type.

Toyota and Honda sell in a median of 24 days vs ~35 for most makes. EVs take 47 days vs ~31 for everything else, and Nissan, Kia, Tesla, Porsche and Lamborghini are the slowest to sell.

🏅Which brand holds its value best?

Rank makes by median Value Retained %. Exclude pre-1990 classics so the comparison is fair.

Lamborghini (52%) and Toyota (48%) top the table, followed by Subaru and Jeep (46%). Nissan (11%), Kia (23%) and Tesla (28%) are at the bottom. Brands that mostly sell EVs suffer most.
